newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan two-month NCD average yield at 7.213 pct.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan two-month NCD average yield at 7.213 pct.

text.p: Taiwan's central bank issued T$3 billion in two-month negotiable certificates of deposit on Friday at an average yield of 7.213 percent, a central bank official said.

The issue came on the same day that Taiwan's stock market saw its dramatic recent bull run halted by profit-taking, with the benchmark index falling 0.37 percent to 9,394.63 on the second-highest turnover in history.

The overnight and short-term money rates soared into double digits in late June as investors diverted holdings into stocks, and have been slowly rising again in the past week to stand well above the central bank's 5.0-5.5 percent target zone.
Some investors had also liquidated their foreign exchange holdings into Taiwan dollars, bolstering the local currency and temporarily halting what had been a slow, steady devaluation.
The currency's value eroded sharply early this week, falling to an eight-year low T$27.994 on Wednesday.
It rallied to T$27.855 on Thursday, only to slip again to T$27.886 shortly before Friday's close.

The central bank has confirmed that it was responding to the liquidity sitution by issuing NCDs to soak up funds, but has denied repeatedly that it was acting directly in response to the stock market bull run.
